children: On Holding will expand its portfolio to include soccer products, inking a deal with Real Madrid forward and French national team captain Kylian Mbappé to be the face of the new category.

Mbappé, the reigning World Cup record goal scorer, will "be at the heart of On's football journey," working directly with the company's product team to develop and test footwear and apparel for the sport, the Swiss company said Friday.
Mbappé will additionally become a global ambassador for the company.

"From the beginning, what drew me to On was the opportunity to build something entirely new together that will help shape tomorrow's game," he said in a statement. "I want to bring my experience and perspective into what we create, push what's possible through innovation, and always stay true to the joy of football."
Mbappé has been associated with Nike since he was young. Nike also is the official supplier for the French national team jerseys.
Mbappé made his pro debut at 16, racking up several French national titles and was a world champion at 19, when France topped Croatia in the World Cup final in Russia during 2018.

He joined Real Madrid in Spain's La Liga from Paris Saint-Germain in the summer of 2024. He captained his France side to a fourth-place finish at the World Cup this year in the U.S., scoring 10 goals at the tournament to take his total tally to 22.

In addition, fellow French countryman and Arsenal legend Thierry Henry will join On Holding as director of football. Henry has been working behind the scenes with the company on its entry and product approach since late 2025, it said. Henry also played for Real Madrid rival Barcelona as well as the New York Red Bulls of Major League Soccer.

The company also said Swiss international and Barcelona player Sydney Schertenleib, who joined On as an ambassador for training and lifestyle, also will expand her relationship with the company and work on product development and testing for the future of the women's game.

On Holding's expansion into the soccer market comes as the company faces slowing sales growth and mounting competition in the sportswear category. The company built its brand around product enhancements and a refusal to discount its shoes and apparel, though today's promotional retail environment is testing that approach.
The company previously said it has no plans to slash prices, even after its weakest retail sales since going public in 2021 forced it to soften its sales outlook last month.
